mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-01.title: Remaining fraction
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-01.body:
The pool got $1 - \frac34 = \frac14$ of the hours: $\frac14 \times 40 = 10$ hours.

**Answer: 10 hours**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-02.title: Ratio parts
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-02.body:
Camp : pool $= 3 : 5$, which is 8 parts for 40 hours, so 1 part $= 5$ hours. Camp 15, pool 25; difference $10$ hours.

**Answer: 10 hours**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-03.title: Only the shift matters
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-03.body:
From week 1 to week 2, 15 hours moved from camp to pool (pool went from 10 to 25). Each moved hour pays $12 - 8 = 4$ dollars more: $15 \times 4 = 60$.

**Answer: \$60**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-04.title: Set the earnings equal
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-04.body:
$8d = 12p$ gives $d = \frac32 p$. Then $\frac32 p + p = 40$, so $p = 16$ and $d = 24$. Each job pays $12 \times 16 = 192$, total $384$ dollars.

**Answer: \$384**

mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-04.title: Inverse ratio
mathcounts-potw-2026-07-20-04.body:
Equal pay means hours are in the inverse ratio of wages: camp : pool $= 12 : 8 = 3 : 2$, so 24 h and 16 h. Earnings: $8(24) + 12(16) = 192 + 192 = 384$.

**Answer: \$384**
